newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares rally on bill, rumors to end higher.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares rally on bill, rumors to end higher.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed sharply higher in hefty trade, boosted by a news report of a draft bill containing Brazil's new telecoms law and hopes the government may exempt stock trade from a new financial tax, brokers said.
"The telecoms bill didn't contain any surprises and the other was just rumors, but the market was ready for any kind of news," a dealer told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded surged 1,012 points, or 1.5 percent, to end at 68,368 on volume of 517 million reais.
Brokers said the rise was spurred by a local Broadcast news agency's report on a draft General Telecommunications Law bill that is expected to go to Congress this week.

While few surprises were revealed, the report sparked a jump in Telebras, whose benchmark preferred ended 1.64 percent higher at 80.80 reais, while its voting common closed up a strong 5.41 percent at 71.89 reais.

Dealers also said bolsa prices rose on comments by top government officials that the CPMF check tax will hurt local financial markets, sparking rumors and speculation Brasilia planned to exempt stock transactions from the new levy.
Brokers said shares had been slightly depressed so a spate of good news was all it took to spark a rally.
"The market was priced waiting for some news," a dealer said, adding Telebras accounted for most of the day's volume.

Apart from Telebras, blue chip rises included state oil firm Petrobras, which climbed 2.79 percent to 147.50 reais, and state power firm Eletrobras, up 1.74 percent to close at 350.00 reais. Cia Vale do Rio Doce saw some light profit-taking on its preferred share on fears the government may delay its privatization. The share fell 0.47 percent to 21.35 percent.
The rise in Eletrobras led an overall rise in the bolsa's wider Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid power shares, which rose 1.24 percent to end at 1,793 points.
